subject: General Science
title: Magnetism and Electromagnetic Induction

outcomes.text: describe the methods of magnetisation and demagnetisation in soft iron,
describe the magnetic field patterns around a magnet,
describe induced electromotive force in electromagnetism,
perform an experiment on electromagnetic induction,
explain factors affecting the magnitude of induced electromotive force,
appreciate the applications of electromagnetic induction in day-to-day life.

content: Factors affecting the magnitude of induced electromotive force (e.m.f) (qualitative treatment)
inquiry_questions: How is the study of electromagnetic induction important in our daily life?
suggested_learning_experiences: Carry out experiments on magnetisation and demagnetisation in soft iron (electrical, induction, hammering and stroking).
Discuss the observations made in the methods to determine the most suitable method of magnetisation.
Carry out experiments on demagnetisation (electrical, hammering and heating).
Utilise online or other available resources to explore the direction of magnetic fields.
Draw the magnetic field patterns around a magnet.
Discuss with peers the meaning of the term “induced electromotive force” in electromagnetism.
Carry out an experiment to demonstrate electromagnetic induction using a U-shaped magnet, galvanometer and a straight conductor.
Use available digital and print media to research on the factors that affect the magnitude of induced electromotive force.
Discuss with peers the ways that electromagnetic induction can be applied in day-to-day life.
Project: Design and make a simple electric bell using locally available materials.
coreCompetencies:
Creativity and imagination: as the learner designs and makes a simple electric bell using locally available materials.
Learning to learn: as the learner carries out experiments of magnetising a magnetic material and demagnetising a magnet.
values:
Unity: as the learner carries out assigned roles when performing experiments to demonstrate electromagnetic induction.
Responsibility: as the learner takes care of the apparatus (U-shaped magnet, galvanometer and straight conductors) while carrying out experiments on electromagnetic induction.
pcis: Life skill (self-esteem): as the learner explains the methods of magnetisation and demagnetisation.
transcription_policy: Source wording retained;line breaks/bullets normalised;pixels authority.
notes: No lesson allocation is stated in this table; do not use the inventory baseline count as an official allocation.

The suggested assessment rubric on printed42–43 gives stationary, parallel, perpendicular-upward and angled conductor movements for an induction demonstration. Independent content review should compare the full procedure against the exact source pixels.

Any electrical magnetisation/demagnetisation or bell circuit requires low-voltage, current-limited teacher-approved apparatus; no mains electricity. Hammering/heating is teacher-controlled with eye/heat protection. The stated factors affecting induced e.m.f. are qualitative, not a numerical derivation.
